core1b.fresh_task: A thin converging lens F=12 cm is followed by a perpendicular plane mirror. With object p=18 cm the central ray retraces; the operator claims all rays strike the mirror normally if the mirror is placed at the image plane. Test the claim, identify the required object position for all paraxial rays to strike normally, and explain whether the mirror distance then matters.
core1b.protected_work: Determine whether the stated all-ray normal incidence and retracing can hold, not just whether the central ray returns.

stages.predict: Before solving, predict the outcome or relationship and record uncertainty.
stages.attempt: A thin converging lens F=12 cm is followed by a perpendicular plane mirror. With object p=18 cm the central ray retraces; the operator claims all rays strike the mirror normally if the mirror is placed at the image plane. Test the claim, identify the required object position for all paraxial rays to strike normally, and explain whether the mirror distance then matters.
stages.reconstruct: p=18 gives q=36 cm, so noncentral rays converge to that plane obliquely. Central ray normal does not imply all rays normal. For all rays normal to perpendicular mirror, output must be axial and parallel, requiring p=F=12 cm. Mirror axial distance does not affect normal incidence for collimated rays, subject to aperture.
stages.diagnose: Only if your saved response exhibits this error: Inferring all-ray retracing from the central ray or a conjugate focus at the mirror. Otherwise record insufficient evidence.
stages.repair: Trace at least two off-axis rays; test their incident directions against the mirror normal.
stages.boundary_test: What if the lens or mirror aperture clips the collimated bundle?
